pre_registered.claim: For Polymarket EPS contracts with an explicit FROZEN strike, betting the side favored by P(round(reported EPS,2) > strike) - where that probability is computed from FRESH consensus (>=3 analysts) plus the firm's cents-model surprise distribution, NOT from our beat-signal blend - is positive-EV net of fees/spread, because the crowd misprices markets whose frozen strike has drifted away from current consensus.
pre_registered.rationale: Our beat-signal disagreements with the market LOSE (-0.57/$1). This bet deliberately does NOT use those signals. It uses consensus (the market's own best estimate) + the frozen strike, exploiting a MECHANICAL mispricing (strike set at creation, consensus drifts) rather than trying to out-predict analysts.
pre_registered.side_rule: YES if contract_prob - yes_price >= min_edge; NO if yes_price - contract_prob >= min_edge
pre_registered.success_criterion: >=30 resolved strike-gap bets AND realized P&L 95% CI-low > 0 AND n >= the live power requirement (forward_test n_needed_at_2.6pct) AND positive after removing the top 5 wins
pre_registered.status: OPEN - RE-BASELINED 2026-11-03, scoring restarts at 0/30 on bets with a verified executable book. NO tradeable claim until success_criterion met on those bets.
pre_registered.prerequisite: contract_prob must be calibrated (synthetic-strike backtest); see output/strike_calibration.txt
pre_registered.honest_notes: No historical Polymarket strikes exist -> this CANNOT be backtested for a money edge; forward vault is the only judge. Do not data-snoop: this exact rule is frozen as written.
pre_registered.rebaselined_2026_11_03: Re-baselined. 41 strike-gap bets had resolved and showed +0.542/$1 (CI [+0.09,+1.05], robust to its top 5). That looks like the success criterion being met — it is NOT, and must not be claimed: the entry gate requires min_executable_edge_after_friction>=0.05 and a live two-sided book, and NONE of those rows recorded the book, so it is unverifiable whether the bets ever met the gate they were registered under. An unverifiable gate is a failed test, not a passed one. Execution context is logged from 2026-11-03 (edge_log: yes_bid/yes_ask/book_spread/depth_usd/max_usd/executable_edge), so scoring restarts from that date at 0/30.
pre_registered.effect_size_assumed: +0.026 per contract (Burgi-Deng-Whelan maker return on >=50c contracts)
pre_registered.power_note: Original criterion '>=30 resolved bets with CI-low>0' is NOT a powered test. At the payoff SD our vault shows, 30 bets cannot separate a real 2.6% edge from zero; a CI that excludes 0 at that n is more likely a tail fluke (this is literally what happened on 2026-10-30). Required n is now computed live by forward_test.required_n(sd, effect) and reported as n_needed_at_2.6pct. Favorites-zone bets need ~2,400; longshot bets ~27,000.

pre_registered.source: PRE-REGISTERED FROM EXTERNAL LITERATURE, NOT FROM OUR OWN RESOLVED BETS. Burgi, Deng & Whelan, 'Makers and Takers: The Economics of the Kalshi Prediction Market' (UCD, Jan 2026), 46,282 contracts / 12,403 events / 2021-Apr 2025: buyers of contracts under 10c lose >60%; contracts above 50c earn a small statistically significant positive return; makers on >=50c earn +2.6% after commission (SD 33%); the bias is worse on the taker side. This matters for provenance: the rule was NOT found by searching our vault, so it is not a multiple-comparisons artifact of our own data.
pre_registered.claim: Restricting to FAVORITE purchases - where the contract we buy costs >= $0.50 (YES costs q, NO costs 1-q) - produces positive realized P&L net of fees and spread, while longshot purchases (cost < 0.50) do not.
pre_registered.side_rule: Only take the side whose contract costs >= 0.50 at entry. Never buy below 0.10.
pre_registered.success_criterion: realized P&L 95% bootstrap CI-low > 0 AND n >= live n_needed_at_2.6pct (~2,400 at the observed favorites SD of 0.65) AND positive after removing the top 5 wins
pre_registered.status: OPEN - forward accumulation from 2026-11-05. NO tradeable claim until powered.
pre_registered.honest_notes: Two caveats kept in writing. (1) The literature's +2.6% belongs to MAKERS; we are a TAKER, the side the same paper shows does worse - so our expected effect is SMALLER than 2.6%, and the required n correspondingly LARGER. (2) Our own favorites subset is currently +0.033/$1 on n=117 with CI [-0.087,+0.148] - consistent with the hypothesis and equally consistent with zero. That subset is PRIOR data and does not count toward this test.

pre_registered.route: C - liquidity provision rather than liquidity taking
pre_registered.claim: Posting fair-value quotes 1c inside the touch on FAVORITE purchases (contract held costs >=0.50) in books with >=$25 of size gets filled often enough to matter, and those fills are NOT adversely selected - i.e. the spread earned is not more than offset by fills arriving when we are wrong.
pre_registered.rationale: Measured on live books the mean spread is 8c while the documented taker edge is 2.6% - the spread is 3.1x the edge and we pay it every trade. Burgi-Deng-Whelan (46,282 Kalshi contracts) find the positive return belongs to MAKERS and the favorite-longshot bias is worse on the TAKER side. This tests whether we have been on the wrong side of the book.
pre_registered.success_criterion: fill rate > 0 AND >=30 resolved fills AND realised P&L 95% bootstrap CI-low > 0 AND positive after removing the top 5 wins
pre_registered.kill_criterion: EITHER >=30 resolved fills with 95% CI-high < 0 (adversely selected), OR >=60 quotes posted over >=3 calendar weeks with ZERO fills. The second case is a REAL FINDING, not an inconclusive one: it means no counterparty will trade with us at these prices and sizes, which closes the maker route as decisively as losing money would.
pre_registered.status: OPEN - paper only, no orders placed, accumulating from 2026-11-05
pre_registered.honest_notes: Fill detection requires the market to CROSS our quoted price and ignores queue position, so measured fill rates are an UPPER BOUND; real fills would be fewer. Spread earned is measured from the mid at quote time. No capital is at risk and no orders are placed.

observed_not_registered._what_this_is: Patterns seen while SEARCHING resolved bets on 2026-11-03. They are NOT results and carry NO weight. ~20 subgroups were tested, so at a 5% level one expects about one false 'significant' slice by chance alone — several of these are probably that. They are written down so that if one is ever promoted to a real hypothesis, it is on record that it came from a search, and it must then be pre-registered and tested on bets that did not exist on 2026-11-03. Do not score these against the data that produced them.

_scoring_rules_2026_11_03: A hypothesis is scored ONLY by forward_test.score_hypothesis(id), which refuses any rule not in pre_registered.
Only bets with logged_at >= scoring_starts_at count. No backward scoring, ever.
Only bets with a verified executable book count (max_usd or depth_usd >= $25).
P&L is computed at the FILL price (ask for YES, 1-bid for NO), never the mid.
Confirmation needs >=30 such bets AND bootstrap CI-low>0 AND a positive mean after removing the top 5 wins.
The success criterion is the one written at registration. Finding a better criterion later voids the test.
A verdict also requires POWER: n >= required_n(sd, 0.026). A CI excluding 0 on an underpowered sample is reported as UNDERPOWERED, not as an edge (added 2026-11-05).

trial_log._why: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (Bailey & Lopez de Prado) and PBO/CSCV both need the NUMBER OF TRIALS to judge whether the best result clears the expected maximum under zero skill. We recorded THAT searches happened but never HOW MANY, which is the input the correction needs. Every subgroup tested, weight fit, or threshold tried is a trial - count it.

trials.what: fill-proxy specification: book-snapshot cross, unrestricted price path, post-quote-restricted price path
trials.outcome: Adopted the post-quote-restricted path on correctness grounds, not because it gave the best number -- it gives 4 fills where the unrestricted version gave 9. Counted as researcher degrees of freedom regardless.

instrument_changes._what_this_is: Changes to how a pre-registered hypothesis is MEASURED, kept separate from its success and kill criteria, which are never amended while it is live. A broken instrument must be fixable without voiding the test, but the fix has to be on the record so nobody can later mistake a measurement change for a result.

changes.what_changed: Fill detection. Was: a once-daily order-book snapshot, counting a fill only when the opposite touch had CROSSED our resting price and the cross still persisted at the moment we polled. Now: that test first, plus a fallback over the minute/hourly price path from /prices-history, restricted to prices AFTER the quote was posted.
changes.why: The snapshot test cannot detect a fill that did not survive until the daily poll, and on the 32-43c spreads we quote it requires the ask to collapse across the whole spread. It reported 0 fills on 10 quotes. The kill criterion's zero-fill branch ('60 quotes over 3 weeks with ZERO fills kills the maker pivot') would therefore have fired on an artifact of the instrument, not on evidence.
two_bugs_found_in_the_fix_itself: The first version queried interval=1w with fidelity=1, which the endpoint answers with HTTP 400. It silently returned [] and the whole fallback was a no-op. Caught by printing the point count instead of trusting that it ran.

The second version searched the full week of history, including prices from BEFORE the quote existed, and reported 9 of 10 quotes filled. Restricting to post-quote prices gives 4 of 10. The unrestricted number would have been a fill booked before we were in the market.
changes.effect_on_the_test: Fill rate goes 0.00 -> 0.40 on the same 10 quotes; mean spread earned 6.79c. The zero-fill kill branch is no longer the operative one. The ADVERSE-SELECTION branch is: >=30 resolved fills with 95% CI-high < 0. That is unchanged and unamended, and stands at 1 resolved fill.
changes.status_of_criteria: UNCHANGED. Neither success_criterion nor kill_criterion was edited.
changes.honest_limit: The price path is a PROXY, not a trade print: Polymarket exposes no public trades endpoint (data-api /trades is 410, CLOB /trades needs auth). A price touching our quote means a counterparty transacted there, not that we were at the front of the queue. Real fills would be LOWER than 40%, never higher, so this biases toward keeping the pivot alive -- which is the direction that costs us more work, not less.

closed_routes._what_this_is: Research routes investigated and CLOSED, with the evidence that closed them. Kept so a route is not re-opened on enthusiasm, and so the reason is auditable rather than remembered.

routes.route: Cross-venue arbitrage, Polymarket vs Kalshi, on earnings EPS
routes.why_it_was_attractive: A price gap on the SAME event is arithmetic, not a forecast. It would have escaped the power problem entirely: no 2,400-bet sample needed, because the edge does not depend on our model being right about anything.
routes.how_it_was_tested: Kalshi's public API needs no key. Walked the full series catalogue (2,400+ series across 12 pages) and then all 25,000 OPEN markets, matching on EPS / earnings per share / quarterly revenue.
routes.result: ZERO company EPS-beat markets on Kalshi. The 265 'earnings'-flavoured series are almost all KXEARNINGSMENTION* -- markets on what a company will SAY on its earnings call, which is an NLP problem on call transcripts, not an EPS outcome and not something our model prices. The 63 apparent non-mention hits were string collisions: 'eps' inside Epstein, DeepSeek and Pepsi. Of 25,000 open markets the single match was a tennis market whose random ID happens to end in EPS.
routes.conclusion: There is no counterpart instrument, so there is no gap to arbitrage. The route is not hard, it is empty. Closed.
routes.cost_of_finding_out: ~30 unauthenticated API calls, no money, one session.
routes.what_would_reopen_it: Kalshi (or another CFTC-regulated venue) listing company EPS contracts on tickers Polymarket also lists. Re-testable by re-running the same catalogue walk; nothing else about the idea needs revisiting.
